title: Angry Birds was not Rovio's first game. It was not their tenth, or their thirtieth.
description:
Angry Birds was not Rovio's first game. It was not their tenth, or their thirtieth.

Three university students who started a company called Relude after winning a Finnish demo competition. It was renamed Rovio two years later.

Rovio had made 51 games and was close to bankruptcy when it built its 52nd, Angry Birds, in eight months. That count comes from Rovio's own company history page, not a rounded up legend.

It is commonly believed the pig enemies were inspired by the 2009 swine flu pandemic, which was in the news while the game was made. Designer Jaakko Iisalo has disputed this, saying the pig design traces back to drawings he made at around age 10, long before the outbreak.

The 51 games and eight month build time both come from Rovio's own company history page. The pig origin is less settled. It survives mainly as a disputed claim, so it is presented here as contested rather than confirmed.

Sources:
- https://www.rovio.com/rovio-history/ - Rovio's own company history page, read in full: confirms the company started in 2003 as Relude, founded by Niklas Hed, Jarno Vakevainen and Kim Dikert after winning a Finnish demo competition, was renamed Rovio in 2005, and had made 51 games and was near bankruptcy before building its 52nd game, Angry Birds, in eight months, released in 2009.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angry_Birds_(video_game) - read in full: confirms it is commonly believed the pig enemies were inspired by the 2009 swine flu pandemic being in the news during development, but that this has since been disputed by designer Jaakko Iisalo, who says the pigs were based on drawings he had made at around age 10.
